answer_key.title: Covenant Remote DCOM Iertutil DLL Hijacking
answer_key.description: This dataset represents adversaries abusing a DLL hijack vulnerability found in the execution of the DCOM InternetExplorer.Application class for lateral movement.

verdict.assessment: A domain user (pgustavo from THESHIRE) was injected into WORKSTATION5 and executed processes across both WORKSTATION5 and WORKSTATION6, while the local wardog user's Microsoft Edge browser data was accessed and backed up to a suspicious directory with Zone.Identifier markers indicating external origin.

findings.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
findings.behavior: RuntimeBroker.exe and browser_broker.exe accessed and created alternate data streams for wardog's Microsoft Edge backup files including database files (spartan.edb), schema data, and cookies, all marked with Zone.Identifier=3 (internet origin).
findings.reasoning: The evidence shows RuntimeBroker.exe and browser_broker.exe accessing and creating Zone.Identifier alternate data streams on Microsoft Edge backup files containing cookies and database files. This represents theft of web session cookies from browser storage, as the processes are reading/accessing cookie backup files (MicrosoftEdgeCookiesBackup.dat) and database files (spartan.edb) that contain session authentication data. The Zone.Identifier marking indicates these are internet-origin files being accessed outside normal browser processes.

findings.name: Distributed Component Object Model
findings.behavior: THESHIRE\pgustavo (domain user) was injected into WORKSTATION5 svchost.exe and spawned multiple processes including rundll32.exe with COM object invocation, taskhostw.exe with suspicious arguments, and cross-host execution to WORKSTATION6 via Internet Explorer.
findings.reasoning: The evidence shows lateral movement from WORKSTATION5 to WORKSTATION6 via COM object invocation (rundll32.exe with SHCreateLocalServerRunDll GUID), followed by remote thread creation and process execution on the target host under the compromised user's context. This is DCOM-based lateral movement, not merely rundll32 abuse for local execution.

findings.name: Verclsid
findings.behavior: verclsid.exe was executed by RuntimeBroker.exe with COM object CLSID parameters and /X flag, invoking {9E175B8B-F52A-11D8-B9A5-505054503030} which is associated with COM marshaling and potential privilege escalation.
findings.reasoning: The evidence shows verclsid.exe being executed with a CLSID parameter and /X flag, which is the canonical abuse pattern for T1218.012. While COM hijacking (T1546.015) requires registry modification for persistence, this event shows direct execution abuse of verclsid as a proxy for code execution, making T1218.012 the most specific and appropriate technique.
